body:
Current MVP promise: a presenter uploads a deck, runs a public Stage plus a private Presenter Console in either (a) Windows extended-display mode or (b) mirrored-display mode with Console on a second device, receives up to 3 evidence candidates within 5s of finalized Korean speech, and explicitly publishes/retracts one audience card. First-demo scope is deliberately narrower: pre-approved public evidence library is publishable; live-web results remain private candidates until measured safe/useful.

Release-blocking success criteria:
1) Privacy: Stage receives 0 bytes of seeded private canaries across HTTP/WSS/DOM/service-worker cache/logs; mirror presentation profile has no Console credential.
2) Display: scripted fresh-user runs succeed on real Windows Chrome/Edge in extend + mirror + single-screen fallback, including popup denied, permission denied, fullscreen exit, monitor unplug, and reconnect. No claim of universal one-click setup.
3) Realtime: duplicate/out-of-order commands apply once; stale controller epochs are rejected; reconnect reaches authoritative snapshot p95 <=2s; command-to-Stage p95 <=300ms target.
4) Evidence: finalized speech -> <=3 eligible Console candidates p95 <=5s on representative Korean corpus. Human approval time is excluded.
5) Publication: only supported/current/pre-approved candidates can publish; a single explicit action publishes, retract always works, slide change makes old card stale; stale/unauthorized/unknown-license/PII candidates are rejected.
6) User value experiment: compared with ordinary slides, measure evidence-finding time, interruption count, Q&A response time, candidate use rate, trust/relevance, and reuse intent with >=10 users. Do not promise broad live-public evidence until false-support and approval-load thresholds pass.

Timeline ladder: security boundary + pre-approved cards -> deck/session sync -> both display modes -> STT/private candidate latency -> RAG/live-web validation -> only then public live evidence; automatic placement and coaching/report are enhancements, not core proof.
summary: Current MVP promise and observable release gates
